defects: ANSWER TO THE QUESTION ASKED -- the 1.0000 saturation of the sign family is a TRUE PROPERTY of the estimand, not a defect in the estimator, and I measured the mechanism rather than inferring it. `_asym(a,b) = (a-b)/(|a|+|b|)` with a = <dlogits(+tv_l), u_hat> and b the same at -tv_l. Two facts force the value. (1) At alpha = 1 the response is linear enough that b = -a to four decimals, so |asym| = 1 exactly -- which is what steering_sign_reversal is FOR, and it correctly reads 1.0000. (2) directional_consistency then degenerates to mean(sign(a)), and a > 0 is forced by the residual stream: tv_{L-1} = tv_l + sum of the blocks above l, so u(tv_l) has positive overlap with u(tv_{L-1}) by construction. Measured cos(u(tv_l), u_hat) at the tested layers -- gpt2 +0.5070 / +0.9108 / +0.9763 / +0.9939 / +1.0000; RANDOM-INIT gpt2 +0.3380 / +0.6310 / +0.8114 / +0.9314 / +1.0000; opt-125m +0.1474 / +0.3108 / +0.6451 / +0.8793 / +1.0000; pythia-70m +0.2955 / +0.4085 / +0.5466 / +0.7506 / +0.7042 / +1.0000; SmolLM2-135M +0.6438 / +0.8451 / +0.3418 / +0.8709 / +1.0000 -- positive at every layer of every model, and just as strongly on the random-init control. The control the quantity actually implements does work: 16 norm-matched RANDOM directions at each of 5 layers give mean asym -0.0617 on trained gpt2 (fraction positive 0.463) and +0.0608 on random-init gpt2 (0.525), against the concept's +1.0. So the column separates a concept direction from an arbitrary one and cannot separate a trained model from an untrained one, because a random-init transformer also has a coherent difference-of-means direction that propagates additively up the residual stream. NOTHING IN THE CODE NEEDS CHANGING TO FIX THIS; the estimand does. To make it training-sensitive the yardstick must be independent of the model's own task vectors -- e.g. project onto a FIXED external concept direction (the difference of unembedding rows for held-out concept-positive vs concept-negative token sets), against which a random-init model has no reason to score 1.0 -- or report the excess over the random-draw null (measured at ~0.06) rather than the raw mean.

THE DE-SATURATION THAT DOES OCCUR IS PARTLY A dtype ARTEFACT, NOT A FINDING. On SmolLM2-135M, dtype='auto' loads bf16 and gives steering_sign_reversal 0.8431 and directional_consistency +0.3569; the SAME weights in float32 give 1.0000 and +0.2000. Layer 7's dir_pos is +10.0632 in bf16 and -20.6192 in float32 -- opposite signs -- and float32 shows it is genuinely wrong-way and linear (-20.6192 / -20.5969 / -20.5103 / -20.4861 / -20.4479 per unit alpha at alpha = 1 / 0.3 / 0.1 / 0.03 / 0.01). Layer 0 is -14.2787 in bf16 against -0.2513 in float32, a 57x inflation of the very number the sign fix was calibrated on (the SIGN is genuine and stable in alpha, so the fix is right; the magnitude is not). pythia-70m fp16 vs fp32 is milder: headline 1.7395 vs 1.7044, sign_reversal 0.9516 vs 0.9631. Since alpha = 1.0 adds a vector of norm ||tv_l|| to a bf16 residual stream, this is a resolution limit, not a bug in this file -- but it means every directional column on a bf16 checkpoint (SmolLM2, Llama, Gemma, Qwen) is dtype-dependent to the point of sign changes. Fix: force the steering forward pass to float32, or emit the dtype and a fp32/native agreement check.

mean_directional_effect and best_directional_effect are unnormalised logit-space magnitudes aggregated across layers that each use a DIFFERENT per-layer yardstick f(tv_l), and are emitted unprefixed. Trained pythia-70m 30.2833 against untrained random-init gpt2 30.8576; gpt2 400.4983 against SmolLM2-135M 130.9534. `best_directional_layer` is 11 on every GPT-2-architecture model trained or not.

A one-line assertion that at a fixed (layer, draw index) the generated vector is bit-identical across samples would pin the matched-denominator property; I had to verify it by hand (seeds 1234 / 24991 / 88343, md5 identical across three samples).

fix_applied: R37: addressed the ESTIMAND finding, not just the estimator. Every directional column projects onto u = W_out*J_ln*v, derived from the model's OWN task vectors, so <D(+tv_l), u> is positive nearly by construction -- cos(u(tv_l), u_hat) is positive at every layer on gpt2 (+0.507..+1.000) and JUST AS POSITIVE on a random-init gpt2 (+0.338..+1.000), which is why the sign family reads 1.0 for trained and untrained alike. Added steering_semantic_effect and steering_semantic_success_rate, projected onto a yardstick defined by the DATA (the tokens distinguishing text_pos from text_neg), so nothing about the direction comes from the activations being measured. Measured: directional_consistency is +1.0000 for trained gpt2 AND both random-init seeds, while the semantic effect gives +0.2762 (succ 1.000) trained vs -0.0313 (succ 0.000) on random-init seed 0. HONESTLY: seed 1 is a false positive (+0.1268, succ 1.000) at the shipped num_samples=3, so this separates on one of two seeds, not two of two -- what it establishes is that the semantic estimand CAN differ between trained and untrained where no existing column could.
